content.title: About
content.content: The chicken fillet sandwich is a popular lunch option in school cafeterias. It consists of tender boiled or baked chicken fillet, a slice of cheese, lettuce, and a sauce placed between two pieces of whole‑grain bread. A nutritious and convenient meal suitable for school‑age children.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken fillet is one of the leanest meat options, low in fat.
School cafeterias often use whole‑grain bread, which provides more fiber than white bread.
Sandwiches are easy to portion and wrap in paper packets for service.
A single sandwich provides about 15–20 g of protein, covering a significant part of a child's daily requirement.
The combination of chicken and vegetables enhances the absorption of B‑vitamins.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken fillet supplies high‑quality protein essential for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, chicken fillet contains less saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from whole‑grain bread
items.content: Whole‑grain bread adds dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The sandwich provides iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of children may be allergic to poultry and need an alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces and cheese can increase salt levels; moderation is recommended.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked and kept at proper temperatures to prevent foodborne illness.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Whole‑grain bread contains gluten, which may be an issue for children with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich can be served warm or at room temperature. It pairs well with fresh vegetables (tomato, cucumber) or a light yogurt sauce. For younger children, cutting it into halves makes it easier to handle.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared sandwich should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 4 hours at +4 °C. For longer storage, keep the components (fillet, bread, vegetables) separate in airtight containers.

rice-white-with-gravy-fat-added.title: White Rice with Gravy and Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: White rice prepared with gravy and added fat is a calorie‑dense side dish commonly found in many cuisines. The rice provides a carbohydrate base, while the gravy and fat give the dish a rich flavor and higher energy content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice loses most of its fiber and micronutrients during milling but retains quickly digestible carbs.
Adding fat (oil or butter) enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins from the gravy.
In some cultures rice with gravy is served as a standalone dish rather than just a side.
Traditional gravies may include tomato base, spices, and sometimes meat broth.
Cooking rice with a large amount of fat can raise the calorie content to about 200–250 kcal per 100 g.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: The fast‑digesting carbs of rice combined with added fat provide a quick energy boost, useful during intense physical activity.

items.title: Improved satiety
items.content: Fat in the gravy slows gastric emptying, helping you feel fuller for longer.

items.title: Source of certain vitamins
items.content: If the gravy is made with vegetable oil, it can contribute vitamin E and some carotenoids.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The added fat makes the dish very calorie‑rich, which may be undesirable for weight management.

items.title: Elevated glycemic index
items.content: White rice has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid spikes in blood sugar.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: If the gravy uses butter or palm oil, saturated fat levels can be high, which is not recommended for heart‑healthy diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice with gravy as a side to meat, fish, or vegetable dishes. It is also used in pilaf‑style preparations or Asian‑style rice with sauce. Adding fresh herbs or a squeeze of lemon can balance the richness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving. Discard if left at room temperature for more than 2 hours due to bacterial growth risk.
